comparison: Perfect agreement on C1-C2. Both evaluations support the viability of zebrafish triple mutants and contrast with mouse lethality. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings by acknowledging the triple mutant line generation as a strength.

Strong agreement on C3-C6 (heart looping and rescue). OpenEval finds quantitative support with adequate statistics. Peer reviewers also address C7-C11 (organ positioning and specification) in the same evaluation, describing experiments as 'rigorous especially with respect to quantification and statistical analysis.'

Agreement on C7-C9 (gata6 expression and organ positioning). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation. Peer reviewers group these claims with heart looping findings (C3-C6) and affirm the left-right patterning defects as convincing.

Agreement on C10-C11 (specification vs. positioning). OpenEval notes the inference could be strengthened with additional markers. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'marker genes sox32 and sox17 were not affected, suggesting Meteorins are required for DFC/KV morphogenesis but not necessarily fate specification.'

Perfect agreement on C34-C36 (transcript degradation and NMD). Both evaluations support the molecular validation of mutants. OpenEval notes direct NMD inhibition would strengthen evidence; peer reviewers implicitly accept by acknowledging the triple mutant targets all known family members.

Perfect agreement on C37-C44 (Nodal-responsive gene expression defects). Both evaluations affirm the quantitative data with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers explicitly mention 'disrupted expression of Nodal-responsive genes' and praise rigorous quantification.

Strong agreement on C46-C61 (spatiotemporal expression of metrn genes in DFCs). OpenEval provides detailed validation of expression patterns. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by acknowledging the functional role in DFC morphogenesis, though they focus more on functional outcomes than expression characterization.

Agreement on C62-C63 (DFC-specific colocalization). OpenEval validates double FISH data. Peer reviewers implicitly support by accepting the DFC-specific functional role, though they don't explicitly discuss the colocalization experiments.

Perfect agreement on C64-C65 (chick expression and evolutionary conservation). Both evaluations support the findings. Peer reviewers note the data is 'compelling but limited to one supplemental figure' and suggest follow-up studies, while OpenEval similarly notes additional species would strengthen conclusions.

Perfect agreement on C66-C70 (DFC clustering defects with maintained identity). Both evaluations affirm the distinction between morphogenesis and specification defects. Peer reviewers explicitly state marker genes were not affected, supporting the maintained identity claim.

Perfect agreement on C71-C75 (DFC migration defects). Both evaluations support the quantitative findings from live imaging and cell tracking. Peer reviewers praise the use of 'timelapse imaging' and rigorous quantification as strengths.

Perfect agreement on C77-C79 (EVL detachment and apical protein mislocalization). Both evaluations affirm the immunohistochemistry data. Peer reviewers explicitly mention 'mislocalization of apical proteins ZO-1 and aPKC, and detachment of DFCs from the EVL.'

Agreement on C84-C87 (KV morphology defects). OpenEval notes significant differences despite high variability. Peer reviewers affirm 'impaired lumen formation' and describe experiments as rigorous with respect to quantification.

Agreement on C89-C91 (KV structure and DFC polarization defects). OpenEval notes quantification would strengthen observations. Peer reviewers group these with other KV defects and provide convincing evidence statement from editor.

Perfect agreement on C92-C97 (reduced fluid flow in KV). Both evaluations support the microsphere tracking and MSD analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly mention 'reduced fluid flow' as one of the key DFC/KV defects identified.

Perfect agreement on C101-C103 (genetic interaction with integrins). Both evaluations affirm the findings. Editor explicitly states 'Meteorins were shown to genetically interact with integrins ItgaV and Itgb1b.' OpenEval notes biochemical interaction remains to be shown.

Perfect agreement on C107-C111 (main conclusions about Meteorin's role in left-right patterning). Both evaluations strongly support these synthesis claims. Editor states authors 'identify an essential role' and 'demonstrate a novel role' while reviewers describe evidence as 'convincing.'

OpenEval evaluates C118 (DFC specification maintained) as supported. No separate peer evaluation found, but this claim overlaps with C66-C70 which peer reviewers explicitly affirm in R7.
